sections.body: Colleges and employers often search applicants online. Your posts, comments and photos can shape first impressions.
Build a positive presence: share your projects, volunteering, writing or creative work. A simple portfolio or professional profile can help.
Review privacy settings regularly, think before posting in anger, and remember that screenshots last even if you delete something.

quiz.q: Which post is most likely to help a future job application?
options: A blog showing a coding project you built
An angry rant about a teacher
hints: A video of you volunteering at an animal shelter would show good qualities. Which option shows skills?
quiz.explain: Sharing a project you built shows skills and initiative.

quiz.q: You post something in anger and delete it 5 minutes later. Is it definitely gone?
options: No, someone may have screenshotted it
Only if it got no likes
hints: Can others save what they see?
If you shout something in a crowded room, you can't un-say it even if you leave.
quiz.explain: No. Others may have screenshotted or shared it before you deleted it.

quiz.q: How often should you review your social media privacy settings?
options: Regularly, because apps and your audience change over time
Only once, when you first sign up
Only if the app sends you a warning
hints: The lesson gives advice on how often to check.
Apps update their features and default settings, and the people who can see your posts change as you grow up.
Worked example: a friend made their account public two years ago for a school project and forgot. Now strangers can see their recent photos and location tags. A setting chosen once didn't fit later.
quiz.explain: The lesson says to review privacy settings regularly. Apps change their features and defaults, and what you're comfortable sharing changes too, so a one-time check can leave old choices in place.
